D1.reasoning: The outcome is the aggregate of votes cast by a large public; no single participant meaningfully controls it.

D2.reasoning: The result emerges from public counting; no closed group knows the certified outcome before the tally is public.

D3.evidenceQuote: certified as the winner by the State X electoral authority
D3.reasoning: No early-knowledge window exists (D2 level 1), so there is no insider to constrain.

D4.evidenceQuote: officially certified as the winner by the State X electoral authority
D4.reasoning: Certification follows a known post-election schedule, though counting duration varies.

D5.reasoning: Manufacturing an election outcome would require fraud at prohibitive cost and legal risk.
